Art Bell has broadcast Halloween ghost story specials on his various paranormal radio shows since 1993. These Halloween specials have become an institution: an annual highlight for oceans of people including myself. Here's a link where most of those episodes can be directly downloaded.

Art Bell retired (again) in December 2015 and this review of the 2016 broadcast of the "Dead Air" Halloween special was Heather Wade's first attempt to fill Art Bells shoes... and I think she did a very good job despite the fact that many of the stores were mediocre!

Detailed Review

I wasn't initially sure how to rate a single "Ghost to Ghost" Halloween special because, over the many years, they've all kinda bled into one nebulous mix of enjoyable anticipation and a handful of awesomely creepy, memorable and well told ghost stories... and a lot of forgettable stories which were enjoyed to hear for the first time because each and every one had the potential to be awesome... but only a handful were noteworthy - a bit like how getting socks wasn't a highlight of your Christmas memories, but still didn't lessen the thrill of unwrapping Christmas gifts when you were a child.

To me, an awesome ghost story is worth an ocean of mediocre ghost stories, but I can't stress enough that even a bad ghost story is fun because while it's being told it has the potential to be great.

I experienced many of the "Ghost to Ghost" shows while on very early morning runs... when the moon and the stars are bright and the shadows are long and the streets are absolutely deserted... sometimes when fog would make shadows from swaying trees look like dancing apparitions.

I recall hearing the story years ago about a mother's little daughter who pointed out the car window as they drove past their local cemetery and said "That's where my imaginary friend lives, under the ground, in a box full of bones." The mother pulled over and asked her daughter to show here where "Elizabeth Grey" (I can't recall the correct name) lives and the little girl took her straight to a grave marked "Elizabeth Gray". The mother asked her daughter when she had visited the graveyard before and the little girl responded "Elizabeth took me here one night".

Another highlight was the Navy officer who told a story about the haunted Aircraft Carrier he was as stationed at. Every nigh-shift crew reported hearing banging and screaming and crying and voices pleading to be let out from within an empty storage room. The hold was sealed because of the number of formal indents which were document... about the room in which seamen burned to death after in years earlier. What made this story creepy was the number of Navy officers who immediately called in afterwards to corroborate the story with very specific details about the specific ship. That was a unexpected joy and super-creepy to hear.

Anyhoo, what I ended up doing was rating each story out of five stars, based purely on how enjoyable it was. Unfortunately this doesn't provide an accurate way for me to compare it to past Halloween specials, but I think it was a good way to arrive at an average score... for the overall show... so here goes:
